At DIVERT we specialise in pallet and polystyrene removal and recycling.
We are 'Landfill Avoidance Specialists!' who endeavour to find pathways to keep as many materials as possible in circulation and out of landfills.
We remove pallets from businesses, taking the good with the bad, ensuring that we leave your space immaculate. We keep pallets in circulation (and out of skip bins and the landfill) by sorting, grading and  repairing them, then finding new homes for them with other businesses. End-of-life pallets and waste wood are deconstructed, then sent for shredding into landscaping mulch.
We also remove and recycle Polystyrene from businesses. We have made a significant investment in a polystyrene compactor, that reduces EPS grade polystyrene to 1/40th of its original size. It is then collected by the tonne by recycling brokers and recycled into other plastics overseas. We are exploring uses within NZ as well; such as emerging technology that should soon allow polystyrene to be used as a substitute for thickening agents in the production of paint.
For now our focus is on preventing polystyrene from filling up our landfills, or worse, breaking down into smaller pieces, being windblown, then being washed down the stormwater drains and out into the Ocean.
Our DIVERT Team are all Site Safety trained and will ensure that we stay clear of your operations and work in with your Health + Safety procedures.  (we also carry public liability insurance)
We offer a professional and reliable service and will do our best to come within 2-3 (working) days of being contacted.

Name: Sunrayker Ltd
Description:
Sunrayker has developed a novel clean energy solution that has successfully combined Concentrated Solar Power and Concentrated Photovoltaics to form a more efficient renewable energy system. After six years of research and development, Sunrayker has proved the concept of a solar receiver that is able to generate electrical energy and thermal energy. Being able to produce both electricity and heat, at the same time, means that the Sunrayker solar energy harvester is extremely efficient. With the high efficiency, the Sunrayker solar energy harvester is able to harvest five times more energy than a fixed flat panel photovoltaic system of a similar size.
The operating temperature of the thermal energy is very high at over 900 degrees Fahrenheit (500°C). This is hot enough to produce high pressure steam that can be used to power a steam turbine that drives a generator to make electricity. The Sunrayker receiver is able to operate at this high temperature without affecting the operation of the photovoltaic solar cells, so the two technologies are able to operate together on the single solar receiver.

Description:
COMMITTED TO QUALITY
Kiwi Charcoal is the first and only sawdust charcoal briquette manufacturing company with operations in the rural Waikato region engaging with the local population for our personnel requirements and adding value to the local economy

Our Goals
- Convert carbon in waste sawdust and dead wood to charcoal – SAVE TREES
- Transform New Zealand from a net importer to exporter of high-quality charcoal logs & briquettes

CHARCOAL IS RENEWABLE
New Zealand currently imports almost all its charcoal of just over 7,000 tons per annum from countries where exhaustible supplies of hardwood are not being properly sustained with replanting and sustainable practices whereas our product is renewable.

Kiwi Charcoal uses the waste of the New Zealand lumber and timber industry as its raw material that is otherwise land-filled where methane production is inevitable. While most landfills in New Zealand are harvesting some of their bio-gas for power production, there is always some gas escaping and contributing to the increase of greenhouse gases which could accumulate as a contribution to anthropological global climate instability.

Kiwi Charcoal has re-designed the anaerobic mechanical process for manufacture of charcoal from sawdust which is more suitable to the New Zealand conditions and raw material of Radiata Pine sawdust available in the country.

Kiwi Charcoal uses not only sawdust, peelings and shavings but even broken logs and small branches commonly abandoned on the lumber camps are also a potential source of raw material available for use without impacting the existing productivity of the mills or loss of a single job to the communities relying on these industries.

Description:
City Energy's mission is to provide affordable heat energy for domestic and industrial applications, with positive environmental outcomes. Due to the material available from New Zealand's sustainable forestry operations, utilisation of biomass for energy is critical to achieve New Zealand's net zero carbon goals by 2050. 

Biomass energy is a natural form of solar energy, absorbing energy from the sun, carbon dioxide is converted into tree mass and stored as potential energy in the tree. The replanting cycle in sustainable forestry means the forest as a whole is in a constant carbon cycle of emission and absorption resulting in a net zero change in total atmospheric carbon dioxide. 

Utilisation of fossil fuels for electricity generation occurs in order to meet peak electricty demand which accounts for around 20% of total electricity generation in New Zealand. Electricity peaks are caused, in part, by heating in winter and electric heat use in households create demand greater than can be supplied by our renewable sources. Turning on the heater or heatpump when our renewable electricity sources are exhausted means 100% of that electricty is generated from fossil fuels. Utilisation of firewood reduces this electricty demand at those critical peaks and replaces it with a renewable energy. There are few legislative barriers for homes to install woodburners and is a simple but powerful way to increase our renewable energy consumption. 

While electricity Process heat uses one third of all energy consumed in New Zealand and a staggering 60% of this is from fossil fuels. Large coal powered boilers used in heating large buildings such as schools and hospitals, and industrial processes such as milk drying and sanitisation plants can be co-fired or converted to biomass through using woodchip instead of coal instantly reducing emissions.

Name: Fibre-gen Instruments Limited
Description:
Fibre-gen’s HITMAN tools are the acknowledged gold standard in nondestructive forest wood segregation technologies optimizing returns to forest owners, timber harvesting companies and wood processing industries around the world.  Fibre-gen designs, manufactures and markets award winning wood grading tools and provides consultation and expertise which allow the non-destructive measurement of wood stiffness throughout the timber supply chain.

“There is huge waste in buying, freighting and processing logs into structural lumber or engineered wood products, only to find the end products fail to meet strength criteria.”

The HITMAN PH330 harvester head acoustic tool is an automated, real-time, wood quality measurement tool for harvesting operations. Its ability to automatically scan and measure the stiffness of a tree stem prior to making a critical log length cutting decision on a processor head is a world first. This system uses scientifically proven and patented acoustic technology to test wood stiffness progressively up a tree stem prior to making log cutting decisions.

Fibre-gen is committed to maximizing wood quality yields from forests and enabling its clients to significantly improve their business returns through the ongoing development, support and application of advanced sonic technology for measuring wood quality.

Name: NZ SDG Summit 2019
Description:
The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals provide an agenda for transforming the world to meet the challenges of ending poverty, enhancing social inclusion, environmental sustainability, peace, good governance and economic prosperity for all countries and peoples. The organising committee are pleased to invite you to join this national, multi-sector Summit on the Sustainable Development Goals – together we are accepting the challenge for our sphere of influence in New Zealand.  

The need for urgency and greater action to progress sustainable development are recognised in the 2019 Summit’s theme of Accelerated action, together.

The purpose of the Summit is to bring together people from all sectors to develop and commit to positive action and accountability on the critical SDGs within our broader spheres of influence. We will do this by providing a platform for recognising, sharing and combining knowledge and skills, and seeking to weave together many threads of accelerated action through preparatory work, keynote addresses, panel discussion and action planning.

The Summit outcomes will be:
•Participants with increased knowledge, skills and tools to act and influence;
•Enhanced commitment and momentum for accelerated action, together beyond the Summit;
•Expansion of key partnerships to deliver accelerated action, and
•An electronic record of the keynote addresses and panel discussions, and the accelerated action plans developed and agreed to within the summit and contributed to by all those who join in.

Ice never stopped a little innovation, and as a country of problem solvers, we dug deep and created a safety solution for those travelling on our roads, walkways and public areas. 

Reach out . . . 

Lighting new avenues and developing with a difference is not just what we’re driven to do – it’s what we’re doing. We may be small in size but we’re big on positive change, turning down the dial on the conventional and igniting the renewable – join us!
